{
  "research_question": "How does the stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance metrics including Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": [
    "Combined",
    "ICMS Only",
    "Dim Visual Only",
    "Bright Visual Only",
    "Sham"
  ],
  "response_variables": [
    "Time-to-Target",
    "Success",
    "Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed",
    "AD"
  ],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "The Combined paradigm yielded the highest success rate (0.7798) and the lowest mean Time-to-Target (2.56 seconds) among all groups.",
    "The Sham group exhibited the poorest performance across all metrics, with the lowest success rate (0.2733), the highest Time-to-Target (4.68 seconds), and the lowest Path Efficiency (0.3084).",
    "Success rates were generally high for visual-only and ICMS-only conditions (ranging from 0.67 to 0.78), but dropped significantly in the Sham condition.",
    "Path Efficiency was highest in the Bright Visual Only (0.5036) and Combined (0.5022) groups, while it was lowest in the Sham group (0.3084).",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) was highest in the Combined group (0.3994) and lowest in the Sham group (0.2360), suggesting the Sham group navigated with less directional variability despite poor overall performance.",
    "Average Speed was highest in the Combined group (12.83) and lowest in the Sham group (10.74), though the difference in speed is smaller relative to the differences in success and time-to-target."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "The most pronounced difference is in the Success metric, where the Combined group (0.7798) and ICMS/Visual-only groups (~0.68-0.78) perform substantially better than the Sham group (0.2733).",
    "Time-to-Target shows a large gap between the Combined group (2.56s) and the Sham group (4.68s), indicating the Sham group takes nearly twice as long to reach the target.",
    "Path Efficiency differs markedly between the Combined/Bright Visual groups (~0.50) and the Sham group (0.31), suggesting the Sham group takes significantly more inefficient paths.",
    "The Combined group has the highest AD (0.3994) compared to the Sham group (0.2360), indicating that while the Sham group is less dispersed, it fails to reach the target efficiently."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "The data suggests that the Combined stimulation paradigm is the most effective for facilitating successful and efficient mouse navigation, outperforming single-modality stimulations (ICMS or Visual) and significantly outperforming the Sham control. The Sham group's low success rate and high time-to-target indicate a severe deficit in navigation capability without stimulation. Interestingly, the Sham group exhibits the lowest angular dispersion, which may imply a rigid, non-adaptive, or stereotyped movement pattern that fails to correct course effectively, leading to the observed inefficiencies.",
  "limitations": [
    "The analysis relies on summary statistics (means and SDs) rather than raw data, preventing the calculation of effect sizes, confidence intervals, or formal statistical significance tests (e.g., ANOVA).",
    "The sample sizes are highly unbalanced across paradigms (Combined n=48,846 vs. Sham n=3,505), which could influence the robustness of mean comparisons if variances differ significantly between groups.",
    "The interpretation of AD (Angular Dispersion) is limited to the provided mean values; without distributional data, it is unclear if the lower AD in the Sham group represents a lack of variability or a systematic bias in movement direction.",
    "No temporal analysis of how performance changes over the course of the experiment is possible with this aggregated data."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables to test for significant differences between the five stimulation paradigms, followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons (e.g., Tukey's HSD) to identify specific group differences and calculate effect sizes (e.g., Cohen's d or eta-squared)."
}
